author: Don Reid
title: Branch County Fairgrounds hosts free Trunk-or-Treat on Saturday - NewsBreak
text:
By Don Reid ,
12 hours ago COLDWATER, MI — The Branch County Fairgrounds turns into a Halloween destination this weekend as the Branch County Fair Board hosts a camping weekend alongside a free Trunk or Treat open to the public.
Trunk or Treat The Fair Board developed Trunk-or-Treat in part to give younger children a more controlled Halloween experience.
Fair Manager Alyssa Blonde says the event offers families a safer, more controlled alternative to going door-to-door on Halloween night.
Now in its third year, the free event has become part of a larger Halloween weekend at the Branch County Fairgrounds.
The Trunk-or-Treat runs from 4:30 to 6 p.m. on Saturday, Oct. 17. Businesses, organizations, and other participants decorate vehicles and hand out candy and trinkets to over 300 to 400 kids.
Blonde encourages people to sign up to host a trunk by calling the fair office.
Hosting a trunk and attending are both free. Blonde notes that most people come in costume.
Attendees enter the fairgrounds at 262 S. Sprague St. The route starts at the horse barns and ends at the Leaders Council clubhouse.
This year's event follows trick-or-treating among the Halloween weekend campers from 3:30 to 4 p.m., connecting the Fair Board's camping program with the free event for the wider community.
Haunted Barn The Haunted Barn is open again from 8 to 10 p.m. on Saturday for $10 per person. This year, it promises even more thrills than last year.
Weekend camping More than 80 people have already signed up to camp with trailers and campers at the Fairgrounds on Friday and Saturday night.
Halloween festivities begin Friday night with a scavenger hunt. Campers enjoy a weekend of seasonal fun for $45 per night.
Friday’s activities feature games and cookie decorating from 6 to 8 p.m., a scavenger hunt at 7 p.m., and a movie night from 8 to 10 p.m. The movie is planned outdoors, with the cabin available as a backup in case of bad weather.
Saturday begins with pumpkin carving and painting at 11 a.m. Pumpkins are provided, and participants bring their own carving or painting supplies.
Campers enjoy their own trick-or-treat session from 3:30 to 4 p.m., just before the public Trunk-or-Treat begins.
The evening continues with a chili and dessert cook-off at 6:30 p.m., followed by live music from An Hour Apart from 7 to 9 p.m.
The weekend wraps up Sunday, Oct. 18, with coffee, cider, and mini donuts at the cabin.
Contact Don Reid, dReid@USATodayCo.Com
